# ChangeTag

A small label for change over time, such as "+3 vs last week". The sign sets the arrow, `goodDirection` sets the tone, and the change is spoken in words. It is never a button.

Also asked as: delta tag, trend indicator.

**Import:** `import { ChangeTag } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.stories.jsx` — Overview, Styles, Formats, CustomIcon, ValueChange, NeverAButton, UnknownValuesFallBack, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `ChangeTag` beside a number to say how it moved since the last period: in
a card header, a table cell or a chart tooltip. For the number itself, use
plain text; for a count on a tab or button, use `CountTag`; for the shape of
a trend, use `Sparkline`.

### Good direction

`goodDirection` says which way is good for this metric. The tone follows from
it, never from the arrow alone.

| Good direction | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Up | More is better: sessions held, reflections completed. Up is success, down is danger. |
| Down | Less is better: no-shows, absences, missed reflections. Down is success, up is danger. |
| None | The change has no value judgment: hours tutored, students assigned. Neutral either way. |

## Best practices

### Set the tone from the metric, not the arrow. {#set-the-tone-from-the-metric-not-the-arrow}

When less is better, up is bad: say so with `goodDirection="down"`.

Do: More no-shows reads as danger.
Don't: More no-shows reads as success.

### Keep a change with no value judgment neutral. {#keep-a-change-with-no-value-judgment-neutral}

Not every change is good or bad. Leave `goodDirection` at `none` for those.

Do: Neutral: more hours is neither good nor bad.
Don't: Success implies a judgment nobody made.

### Never make a change tag a button. {#never-make-a-change-tag-a-button}

It renders a `span` with no role and no click handler: `onClick`, `role` and
`tabIndex` are dropped with a console warning in development.

## Accessibility

- **The change is spoken in words.** A screen reader hears "Up 3 vs last
  week" or "Down 12% vs last month"; the visible chip and comparison are
  `aria-hidden`, so nothing is read twice.
- **Color never carries it alone.** The arrow and the sign say the direction;
  the tone only reinforces it.
- **Not a control.** No role, no tab stop, no click handler.
- **Reduced motion.** The fade and the color change read the motion duration
  tokens, which drop to 0ms when reduced motion is on.

## Related

- For a count on its own, use `CountTag`.
- For the condition something is in, use `StatusTag`.
- For the shape of a trend beside a number, use `Sparkline`.

Same group: `AiMessage` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `PromptStarters` · `SmartTag` · `StatusTag` · `Suggestion` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Arrow.** Up, down or flat, from the sign of `value`. `iconBefore` replaces it. It is decoration; the value and the spoken text say the direction.
2. **Value.** Signed: "+3", "−12%", "+4.5 pts". An em dash when there is nothing to compare.
3. **Chip.** A filled ground in the tone, with a 1 inside border, so the height stays exact.
4. **Comparison.** Optional, such as "vs last week", in subtle text after the chip.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. The tone (neutral, success, danger) comes from the sign and `goodDirection`. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. It is a label, not a control. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A label is never dimmed. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Height | `--label-height-md` (20), or `--label-height-sm` (16) when compact. |
| Padding and gap | `--pad-x-xs` on both sides, 2 between arrow and value, `--inline-sm` before the comparison. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`. |
| Neutral | `--ds-background-neutral` fill, `--ds-text` words, `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` edge. |
| Success | `--ds-background-success` fill, `--ds-text-success` words, `--ds-background-success-pressed` edge. |
| Danger | `--ds-background-danger` fill, `--ds-text-danger` words, `--ds-background-danger-pressed` edge. |
| Comparison | `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Motion | `--motion-duration-medium`, with `--motion-easing-entrance` for the value and `--motion-easing-standard` for the color. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the period: "vs last week", "vs last term". | Leave a change with no baseline when the period is not clear from the page. |
| Pass the raw signed number: `value={-12}` with `format="percent"`. | Pass a formatted string such as "-12%". |
| Use `null` when there is nothing to compare. | Show 0 for a missing comparison: 0 means no change. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | — | The signed change. Above zero is up, below is down, zero is flat; `null` shows an em dash and reads "No change data". |
| `format` | enum | `'number'` | `number` (+3), `percent` (+12%) or `points` (+3 pts). Always signed. |
| `goodDirection` | enum | `'none'` | Which way is good: `up` or `down` turn the tag success or danger; `none` keeps it neutral for a change with no value judgment. |
| `comparison` | node | — | What the change is measured against, such as "vs last week", in subtle text after the tag. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` (20) in cards and headers; `compact` (16) in table cells. |
| `iconBefore` | string or node | — | Replaces the direction arrow: a Font Awesome Free name (`arrow-trend-up`) or a node. Decorative; the words carry the direction. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the tag element beside the component's own. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the tag element. |

## Variants

**`format`** — `number` · `percent` · `points`

**`goodDirection`** — `up` · `down` · `none`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
